learn.hook: Democracy is like a school report card: we judge it by its results. What should we expect, and how do we measure it?
points: Democracy is preferred because it promotes equality among citizens, enhances the dignity of the individual, improves the quality of decision-making, provides a method to resolve conflicts, and allows room to correct mistakes.
Democracy only creates conditions for achieving goals; citizens must use those conditions. Its outcomes should be judged against realistic expectations.

An accountable government: citizens have the right and the means to examine the process of decision-making. This is called transparency. Democracy ensures decisions are taken according to rules and procedures.
Decisions in a democracy may be slower because of discussion and negotiation, but they are more acceptable to people and more effective. The cost of time is worth it.

A democratic government is a legitimate government — it may be slow, less efficient or not always responsive, but it is the people's own government. Regular, free and fair elections, open public debate and citizens' right to information help keep it accountable and responsive.

example.q: Think it through: A dictator builds a road in one month; a democratic government takes six months after public meetings. Which decision is better in the long run?
steps: The dictator's decision is quick, but people had no say and may not accept it.
The democratic process is slow, but people were consulted, so the decision is more acceptable.
Acceptable decisions are carried out more effectively and are less likely to cause conflict.
example.answer: The democratic decision is often better in the long run because it is more acceptable and effective, even if slower.

learn.reallife: Under the Right to Information, any citizen can ask a government office for information about how a decision was made — a tool of transparency.

games.title: True or false: democratic government
items: Transparency means citizens have the right and the means to examine the process of decision-making.
This is how democracy makes government accountable.
Democratic decisions are always faster than those of non-democratic governments.
Democracy involves discussion and negotiation, so decisions may take more time.
A democratic government is the people's own government, which makes it legitimate.
Its legitimacy comes from the people.
Democracy by itself guarantees every good outcome without citizens doing anything.
Democracy creates conditions; citizens must use them to achieve goals.
Democracy provides room to correct mistakes.
Public debate and elections allow wrong decisions to be reviewed and changed.

games.title: Match the idea
pairs: Citizens can examine how decisions are made
People accept it as their own government
Regular chance to change the government

quiz.q: What does 'transparency' mean in a democracy?
options: Citizens have the right and the means to examine the process of decision-making
Decisions are made by one person
quiz.explain: Transparency lets citizens check whether decisions were taken according to proper rules and procedures.
steps: Asked: the meaning of transparency.
Transparency: citizens have the right and the means to examine the process of decision-making.
So they can check if decisions followed rules and procedures.
Secrecy is the opposite.
Answer: Citizens have the right and the means to examine the process of decision-making
quiz.mistake: Confuses transparency with secrecy or speed

quiz.q: Why may decisions in a democracy take more time?
options: Because they involve discussion, deliberation and negotiation
quiz.explain: Democracy is based on consultation, so it takes time, but the decisions are more acceptable.
steps: Asked: why democratic decisions may take more time.
Democracy is based on discussion, deliberation and negotiation.
This takes time, but the decisions are more acceptable and effective.
Answer: Because they involve discussion, deliberation and negotiation
quiz.mistake: Thinks delay in democracy is only a weakness

quiz.q: Which outcome can democracy be expected to produce most clearly?
options: The fastest economic growth in the world
A government that is accountable to citizens and responsive to their needs
quiz.explain: The most basic outcome of democracy is an accountable, responsive and legitimate government.
steps: Asked: the outcome democracy most clearly produces.
Democracy only creates conditions; outcomes must be judged realistically.
Its basic outcome is an accountable, responsive and legitimate government.
Fastest growth, no poverty or equal incomes are not guaranteed.
Answer: A government that is accountable to citizens and responsive to their needs
quiz.mistake: Expects democracy to solve every economic problem automatically

quiz.q: Why is a democratic government called 'legitimate'?
options: Because it is the fastest government
Because it is chosen by the army
Because it is the people's own government
quiz.explain: Even if slow or imperfect, a democratic government has the people's support, so it is legitimate.
steps: Asked: why a democratic government is legitimate.
It may be slow, less efficient or not always responsive.
But it is the people's own government, so it is legitimate.
quiz.mistake: Thinks legitimacy depends on efficiency

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a reason why democracy is considered better than other forms of government?
options: It guarantees that decisions are taken very quickly
It enhances the dignity of the individual
It provides a method to resolve conflicts
quiz.explain: Democracy does not promise speed; its strengths are equality, dignity, better decisions, conflict resolution and room to correct mistakes.
steps: Asked: which item is NOT a reason democracy is better.
Reasons: equality, dignity, better decisions, a method to resolve conflicts, room to correct mistakes.
Democracy does not guarantee quick decisions; they may be slower.
So 'decisions are taken very quickly' is not a reason.
quiz.mistake: Assumes speed is one of democracy's strengths

quiz.q: What does democracy do, according to the textbook view of outcomes?
options: It solves all problems on its own
It creates conditions for achieving goals, which citizens must use
It removes the need for citizens to participate
quiz.explain: Democracy is a form of government that creates conditions; citizens have to take advantage of them.
steps: Asked: what democracy does, in the textbook view.
Democracy creates conditions for achieving goals.
Citizens must use those conditions; it does not solve everything on its own.
Answer: It creates conditions for achieving goals, which citizens must use
quiz.mistake: Treats democracy as a magic solution

quiz.q: Which practice helps make a democratic government accountable?
quiz.explain: Elections let citizens reward or remove governments, making them answerable to the people.
steps: Asked: a practice that makes government accountable.
Regular, free and fair elections let citizens reward or remove governments.
Banning newspapers, postponing elections or secret files weaken accountability.
Answer: Regular, free and fair elections
quiz.mistake: Picks a practice that weakens accountability

quiz.q: What does 'democracy provides room to correct mistakes' mean?
options: Mistakes never happen in a democracy
Mistakes are hidden from the public
Wrong decisions can be discussed publicly and changed
quiz.explain: Public debate, a free press and elections allow mistakes to be noticed and corrected.
steps: Asked: the meaning of 'room to correct mistakes'.
Democracy has public debate, a free press and elections.
So wrong decisions can be discussed publicly and changed.
It does not mean mistakes never happen.
Answer: Wrong decisions can be discussed publicly and changed
quiz.mistake: Thinks democracy is free of mistakes

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'Democracy is slow. So why do people still prefer it?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Slower but accountable, transparent and legitimate — the people's own government!
teach.nudge: Good! What does transparency mean, and why are democratic decisions more acceptable?

revise.summary: The most basic outcome of democracy is a government that is accountable, responsive and legitimate. Democratic decisions may be slower, but they are more acceptable and effective.
focus: The meaning of transparency and accountability
Why slower decisions can be better
Why a democratic government is legitimate
remember: Transparency: citizens have the right and the means to examine the process of decision-making
Democracy creates conditions for achieving goals; citizens must use them
Legitimate government: it is the people's own government
traps: Speed is not one of democracy's strengths
Don't treat democracy as a magic solution to every problem
Legitimacy does not depend on efficiency

learn.hook: If democracy is the people's government, will it make everyone rich and equal? The honest answer is: not automatically.
points: Studies show dictatorships have had a slightly higher rate of economic growth than democracies, but the difference is negligible. Democracy cannot simply be blamed for slow growth.
Economic development depends on several factors: the country's population size, the global situation, cooperation from other countries and the economic priorities adopted by the country.
Even if growth is slightly lower, democracy is preferable because it has many other positive outcomes like dignity, accountability and freedom.

Democracies are based on political equality — every adult citizen has one vote with equal value. Yet economic inequality remains: a small number of ultra-rich people enjoy a large share of wealth and income, while those at the bottom have very little.

Since the poor are a large part of the voters, one might expect democracies to focus on reducing poverty. But democracies do not appear to be very successful in reducing economic inequalities, and in many countries people still lack basic needs.

example.q: Think it through: Every citizen has one vote of equal value. Why does economic inequality still continue in democracies?
steps: Political equality (one person, one vote) is not the same as economic equality.
Many factors beyond voting decide incomes, such as growth, opportunities and government priorities.
So equal votes do not automatically produce equal incomes.
example.answer: Because political equality does not by itself guarantee economic equality.

learn.reallife: Every voter in a city — whether living in a big bungalow or a small rented room — gets one vote of equal value on election day, yet their incomes may be very different.

games.title: Fill the gap: growth and equality

items.text: Dictatorships have had a slightly ___ rate of economic growth than democracies, but the difference is negligible.
In a democracy every adult citizen has one ___ with equal value.
Equal votes are called political equality, but ___ inequality can still remain.
Economic development depends on population size, the ___ situation, cooperation and economic priorities.

games.title: True or false: democracy and the economy
items: Democracies have always had much faster economic growth than dictatorships.
Dictatorships had a slightly higher growth rate, though the difference is negligible.
Economic development depends on factors like population size and the global situation.
These factors affect growth regardless of the type of government.
Political equality means every adult has one vote of equal value.
This is a basic principle of democracy.
Democracy has completely removed economic inequality in every country.
Economic inequalities still exist in democracies.
Democracy is preferred even with slightly lower growth because of its other positive outcomes.
Dignity, freedom and accountability matter too.

quiz.q: What do studies show about economic growth in dictatorships compared to democracies?
options: Dictatorships grow slightly faster, but the difference is negligible
quiz.explain: The difference in growth rates is very small, so democracy cannot be blamed for slow growth.
steps: Asked: growth in dictatorships vs democracies.
Studies show dictatorships grew slightly faster.
But the difference is negligible, so democracy cannot be blamed for slow growth.
Answer: Dictatorships grow slightly faster, but the difference is negligible
quiz.mistake: Assumes democracy always gives the fastest growth

quiz.q: Which of these does economic development of a country NOT mainly depend on, according to the chapter?
options: The colour of the national flag
quiz.explain: Development depends on population size, the global situation, cooperation from other countries and economic priorities.
steps: Asked: which item development does NOT depend on.
Development depends on population size, global situation, cooperation of other countries and economic priorities.
The colour of the national flag has nothing to do with it.
quiz.mistake: Does not recall the factors behind development

quiz.q: Why is democracy still preferred even if its growth rate is slightly lower?
options: Because it has many other positive outcomes like dignity, freedom and accountability
Because it guarantees that nobody is poor
Because it does not hold elections
quiz.explain: Democracy is valued for much more than growth alone.
steps: Asked: why democracy is preferred despite slightly lower growth.
Democracy has many other positive outcomes.
These include dignity, freedom and accountability.
It does not guarantee that nobody is poor.
Answer: Because it has many other positive outcomes like dignity, freedom and accountability
quiz.mistake: Judges a government only by its growth rate

quiz.q: What is 'political equality' in a democracy?
options: Every adult citizen has one vote with equal value
quiz.explain: Each adult citizen's vote counts the same; this is political equality.
steps: Asked: the meaning of political equality.
Every adult citizen has one vote with equal value.
Equal income or land is economic equality, which is different.
Answer: Every adult citizen has one vote with equal value
quiz.mistake: Confuses political equality with economic equality

quiz.q: Which statement about economic inequality in democracies is correct?
options: A small number of ultra-rich people enjoy a large share of wealth, while those at the bottom have very little
quiz.explain: Democracies have not been very successful in reducing economic inequality.
steps: Asked: the correct statement about economic inequality in democracies.
A small number of ultra-rich people enjoy a large share of wealth and income.
Those at the bottom have very little.
So inequality has not been removed.
Answer: A small number of ultra-rich people enjoy a large share of wealth, while those at the bottom have very little
quiz.mistake: Believes democracy automatically ends inequality

quiz.q: Why might one expect democracies to work hard to reduce poverty?
options: Because the poor are a large part of the voters
Because poor people form the government alone
Because elections are only held in villages
quiz.explain: Since the poor are a large share of the electorate, no party would want to lose their votes.
steps: Asked: why democracies might be expected to reduce poverty.
The poor are a large part of the voters.
So parties would not want to lose their votes.
Answer: Because the poor are a large part of the voters
quiz.mistake: Does not link votes with policy priorities

quiz.q: Which outcome can democracy NOT be said to have guaranteed so far?
options: The right of citizens to vote
quiz.explain: Democracies have regular elections and legitimate governments, but economic inequality persists.
steps: Asked: an outcome democracy has NOT guaranteed.
Democracies have regular elections, legitimate governments and the right to vote.
But they have not been very successful in reducing economic inequality.
So an end to economic inequality is not guaranteed.
quiz.mistake: Thinks reducing inequality is an assured outcome of democracy

quiz.q: A student says, 'Democracy is useless because growth in my country is slow.' What is the best response?
options: She is right; only growth matters
Growth depends on many factors besides the type of government, and democracy has other important outcomes
quiz.explain: Slow growth may be due to many factors; democracy should be judged on all its outcomes.
steps: Asked: the best response to 'democracy is useless because growth is slow'.
Growth depends on many factors: population, global situation, cooperation, priorities.
The growth gap with dictatorships is negligible.
And democracy has other important outcomes like dignity and freedom.
Answer: Growth depends on many factors besides the type of government, and democracy has other important outcomes
quiz.mistake: Blames democracy alone for every economic problem

teach.ask: Gappu flaps: 'Doesn't democracy make everyone rich and equal? Why not?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Growth depends on many factors and inequality remains — but democracy still brings dignity and accountability!
teach.nudge: Nice! How do growth rates compare with dictatorships, and does one vote each mean equal incomes?

revise.summary: Dictatorships have grown only slightly faster than democracies, a negligible difference, and development depends on many factors. Democracies give political equality but have not been very successful in reducing economic inequality.
focus: What studies show about growth in dictatorships and democracies
The factors on which economic development depends
remember: Development depends on population size, the global situation, cooperation from other countries and economic priorities
Political equality: every adult citizen has one vote with equal value
traps: Don't blame democracy alone for slow growth
Political equality is not economic equality
Democracy has not guaranteed an end to economic inequality

topics.title: Social diversity, dignity and freedom of citizens

learn.hook: A good democracy is like a big family get-together: different tastes, different opinions, but everyone gets a seat at the table.
points: Democracies usually develop a procedure to conduct their competition peacefully, which reduces the chance of tensions turning violent. Belgium is a good example of successfully negotiating differences among groups.

Two conditions are needed: majority and minority opinions must work together (democracy is not simply rule by majority opinion), and rule by majority must not become rule by the majority community in terms of religion, race or language. Anyone should be able to be part of the majority at some point.
Dignity and freedom: democracy is far better than any other form of government in promoting the dignity and freedom of the individual. Every person wants respect from others.

Dignity of women: in most societies women were long treated as unequal. Democracy accepts in principle that women are equal, legally and morally, so their struggle for equal treatment now has support.

Caste: democracy has strengthened the claims of disadvantaged and discriminated castes for equal status and equal opportunity. Expectations from democracy keep rising, and people complaining about it is itself proof of its success — they have become aware and able to judge the government critically.

example.q: Think it through: People in a democracy complain loudly about their government. Is this a sign of failure?
steps: Complaining shows people expect a lot and are aware of their rights.
They feel free to look critically at those in power.
People who were once subjects have become citizens who judge their rulers.
example.answer: No. The fact that people complain is itself a testimony to the success of democracy.

learn.reallife: When a woman sarpanch leads a gram sabha in Rajasthan or a first-generation student becomes an IAS officer, you see democracy widening dignity and opportunity.

games.title: Steps from difference to peaceful solution
games.prompt: Arrange how a democracy handles a disagreement between groups
items: Groups voice different demands openly
Representatives discuss and negotiate
A decision acceptable to all sides is reached
The decision is carried out and can be reviewed later

games.title: Healthy democracy or warning sign?
items: Majority and minority work together
Anyone can be part of the majority at some time
Rule by majority becomes rule by one religious community
Women's claims for equality get legal support
A group is permanently kept out of power because of its birth
Citizens freely criticise the government

quiz.q: Which condition is necessary for democracy to accommodate social diversity?
options: Rule by majority must not become rule by the majority community in terms of religion, race or language
Only the majority community should hold power
quiz.explain: Democracy requires that majority rule is not the permanent rule of one community.
steps: Asked: a condition for accommodating social diversity.
Rule by majority must not become rule by the majority community in religion, race or language.
Majority and minority opinions must also work together.
Answer: Rule by majority must not become rule by the majority community in terms of religion, race or language
quiz.mistake: Equates democracy with permanent majority rule

quiz.q: What does 'democracy is not simply rule by majority opinion' mean?
options: Majority and minority opinions need to work together
quiz.explain: The majority must work with the minority so that the government represents general views.
steps: Asked: the meaning of 'not simply rule by majority opinion'.
Majority and minority opinions need to work together.
So the government represents general views, and the majority cannot ignore the minority.
Answer: Majority and minority opinions need to work together
quiz.mistake: Thinks democracy means the majority can ignore the minority

quiz.q: Which country is the textbook example of successfully negotiating differences among social groups?
quiz.explain: Belgium accommodated its language communities through power sharing.
steps: Asked: the textbook example of negotiating differences among groups.
Belgium accommodated its language communities through power sharing.
Sri Lanka followed majoritarian policies, so it is not the example.
Answer: Belgium
quiz.mistake: Forgets the Belgium case from the first chapter

quiz.q: How has democracy affected the struggle of women for equal treatment?
options: It has banned women from public life
It treats women as legally unequal
It accepts in principle that women are equal, so their struggle has legal and moral support
quiz.explain: Because democracy accepts equality in principle, women's demands for equal treatment gain support.
steps: Asked: democracy's effect on women's struggle for equality.
Democracy accepts in principle that women are equal, legally and morally.
So their struggle for equal treatment now has support.
Answer: It accepts in principle that women are equal, so their struggle has legal and moral support
quiz.mistake: Assumes democracy has already achieved full gender equality, or nothing at all

quiz.q: What has democracy done for disadvantaged and discriminated castes in India?
options: Strengthened their claims for equal status and equal opportunity
quiz.explain: Democracy has given these groups a stronger basis to claim equal status and opportunity, though inequalities remain.
steps: Asked: what democracy did for disadvantaged castes.
Democracy strengthened their claims for equal status and equal opportunity.
Inequalities remain, so it did not end caste differences completely.
Answer: Strengthened their claims for equal status and equal opportunity
quiz.mistake: Thinks democracy has either done nothing or completely ended caste inequality

quiz.q: What does it show when people in a democracy complain about their government?
options: That people are aware and can look critically at those in power — a sign of democracy's success
That people do not want democracy
quiz.explain: Complaints show that people have become aware citizens who expect a lot from democracy.
steps: Asked: what people's complaints in a democracy show.
People have become aware and can judge those in power critically.
Expectations from democracy keep rising.
So complaining is itself a sign of democracy's success.
Answer: That people are aware and can look critically at those in power — a sign of democracy's success
quiz.mistake: Reads complaints only as a sign of failure

quiz.q: In which area is democracy considered far better than any other form of government?
options: Promoting the dignity and freedom of the individual
quiz.explain: Democracy's clear strength is respect for individual dignity and freedom.
steps: Asked: where democracy is far better than other forms of government.
Democracy is far better in promoting the dignity and freedom of the individual.
Its record on growth and equal incomes is mixed, and decisions can be slow.
Answer: Promoting the dignity and freedom of the individual
quiz.mistake: Mixes up democracy's clear strengths with areas where its record is mixed

quiz.q: Why should anyone be able to become part of the majority at some point in a democracy?
options: So that the same community always wins
So that elections are not needed
So that minorities lose their rights
So that no group is permanently excluded from power because of its birth
quiz.explain: If a group could never be in the majority because of its religion, language or caste, democracy would stop being fair to it.
steps: Asked: why anyone should be able to join the majority at some point.
If a group can never be in the majority because of its religion, language or caste, it is permanently excluded.
Democracy would then stop being fair to it.
So no group should be shut out of power because of birth.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the danger of a permanent majority based on birth

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How does democracy keep people of different groups happy and respected?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Majority and minority together, dignity for women and all castes — that's democracy's best gift!
teach.nudge: Good! Can you say why majority rule must not be rule by one community, and how democracy helps dignity?

revise.summary: Democracy helps societies handle social diversity peacefully and is far better than other forms of government at promoting individual dignity and freedom. People complaining about it is itself a sign of its success.
focus: The two conditions for democracy to accommodate social diversity
How democracy supports the dignity of women and disadvantaged castes
remember: Democracy is not simply rule by majority opinion; majority and minority must work together
Rule by majority must not become rule by the majority community in terms of religion, race or language
Belgium: example of successfully negotiating differences among groups
traps: Don't equate democracy with permanent majority rule
Don't read complaints only as a sign of failure
Don't say democracy has ended gender or caste inequality, or that it has done nothing; it has strengthened claims to equality
